$comment: The cli's words, as data: every code with what a person or an agent reads (a short is at most 80 characters), and the lines its verbs say, by verb. A {slot} is filled by the code that says the line; contracts/codes.cjs is their one door.
codes: the package is present but does not load
a package could not answer a question about its stores; what it holds stays, and is named
telemetry could not give its hint line, so none is said
empty here, not a problem: the server stays wired and lists a tool once it holds a record
DecisionBook could not say what is protected, so no line is said
a package manifest has the wrong shape
the arguments of this verb have the wrong shape
this flag takes a value and none was given
this verb does not take this flag; nothing was done
a JSON draft is read only from {drafts} in the repository, by --file and with no JSON word beside it; nothing was done
not inside a git repository; run git init here first, or name one with --target
no folder is there; name a folder of your repository with --target
this is the product itself, not a repository to wire
a home or temp directory is not a project, even with a .git in it; nothing was written; run this in the repository, or name it with --target
the install path holds a character no quoted shell command can carry; reinstall elsewhere
a host configuration file is not the expected JSON; fix it, nothing was overwritten

git tracks this file, and it is one machine's own record of what setup wrote there, so nothing it lists is trusted and nothing here was changed or removed: take it out of git (git rm --cached, then commit) and run this again
a file of yours is at a path where setup writes its own, so setup wrote nothing at all: move or rename yours and run it again
a file from an unknown major version
the host sent something that is not a hook event
a hook handler failed with an uncoded error
a hook handler did not answer in time
a handler or the port's own step failed; the reply's note names which and its code
a gate formed no verdict on this write, so it asks: allow it only if you meant it
a hook call that carries the person's words came from the AI host itself: the host holds the other end of its output
a hook call that carries the person's words was heard on a platform where its caller cannot be told: a named limit

this hook call carries a person's words and did not come from the AI host itself (the host holds the other end of its hook's output), so no one heard it and nothing was recorded as the person's: theirs is only what they send in the session
the hook event that carries the person's words is called by the AI host alone: a shell command naming it does not run
a verb, hook or MCP tool the product promises has no code that answers it
stopped by a signal; what was recorded stays and nothing runs on
a background child past the bound its starter gave it ended itself; its verb ran no further
a package's first run at setup failed; the wiring is done
a link in its path refused this one write, the rest is installed; to have this file too, make that folder a real one and run setup again
a settings file that came with this repository lets your AI host act without asking you; setup did not write these rows, so read them before you trust this folder
.mcp.json is tracked, and it now names this machine's node and install: do not commit that change; a teammate runs atlasbound setup for their own
setup could not read what a commit brought in the host files; the wiring is done
setup could not ask git which of its files git would show; the wiring is done
uninstall could not ask git which host files came with it, so it left our lines in every one of them
git would show these files setup wrote and keeps out of git (the settings and .mcp.json name this machine's paths): commit none of them; the rule in brackets brings each back
nothing was written; atlasbound protect lists what you could choose
not a store this version writes: you or another tool put it here
nothing was written; atlasbound modules names every module and which are on here
a hook row of a module that is off here: it does nothing; only the person turns the module back on, in a terminal of their own: atlasbound modules on <name>
a verb of a module that is off here: it answers the module's one line and writes its own trace row, nothing else
your data stays: only the hook rows, commands, MCP servers and allow rules setup wrote went
what this repository left in your home (your words among them); atlasbound uninstall --purge removes it
the store of a product package that is not installed here
the phrase was not typed as shown, so nothing was done
only a person may run this, at a plain terminal of their own: ask them to type the command above; nothing was done
a program that can type for a person stands above this terminal, and this act takes a protection away: run the command above in a plain terminal window; nothing was done

a verb only a person runs, so a shell command that names it, bare or through a wrapper, does not run: ask the person to type it with its words in a terminal of their own. A guard for an AI that works in the open, not a sandbox: atlasbound debug who shows each such act and who ran it
AtlasBound's own file, or a host settings file that can switch its hooks off

It holds hook rows, allow rules, the .gitignore block, a slash command or records, which only AtlasBound's own commands change (setup, protect, decisionbook), or it is the AI host's settings, where one line turns every hook off; allow this only if you asked for this very change.
the earlier version's server still runs, so leftovers remove took nothing; the person ends it
the process listing did not answer, so leftovers remove took nothing: the earlier server may still run
a person acts: a terminal with no AI session mark and no AI host above it
the AI acts in a session that holds a person's prompt; the row names its time
the AI acts and nothing shows a person behind it; could not tell reads the same
the package that declares the MCP server exports no handshake text to start it with, so debug inject cannot measure it; nothing was written

leftovers.verb: list what an AtlasBound from before {version} left in your home: hook rows, an MCP server, its sign-in key and send logs
leftovers.takeOut: to take them out: atlasbound leftovers remove (you, at your own terminal); it keeps a copy of each first
leftovers.noHome: this user has no home to look in
leftovers.unlisted: the system's listing of the running processes did not answer, so the earlier version's server may still run here
leftovers.closeFirst: close every AI session opened before the upgrade (or end those PIDs yourself): an open one keeps the earlier version's server running in memory, and that server writes its files back
leftovers.running: pid {pid}: the earlier version's MCP server, still running in memory: {line}
leftovers.hooks: {at}: {n} hook rows run the earlier version's hooks folder, which {version} does not have: every AI session meets a failing hook
leftovers.server: {at}: an MCP server named {server} ({where}), which {version} does not have
leftovers.engine: atlasbound's earlier engine from a folder that is no installed package, left alone
leftovers.store: ~/{store}: the earlier version's event store ({n} folders: one per repository, and its own); nothing here takes it: delete the folder yourself once no earlier version runs
leftovers.processesUnread: the running processes (the system's listing did not answer)
leftovers.head: atlasbound leftovers: {what}
leftovers.left: what an AtlasBound from before {version} left
leftovers.noneBeside: nothing from before {version} is left to take out; what is named below is left alone
leftovers.stillRuns: the earlier version's server still runs here (pid {pids})
leftovers.notTaken: atlasbound leftovers remove: nothing was taken: {why}
leftovers.again: then run atlasbound leftovers remove again
leftovers.tookHead: atlasbound leftovers remove: took out what an AtlasBound from before {version} left
leftovers.copied: a copy of each is in ~/{backup}; delete that folder once you are sure
leftovers.restart: restart every AI session: each reads its settings again, and one opened before the upgrade keeps the earlier version's server running in memory until it is closed
leftovers.machine: kept ~/{store}, this user's for every repository: {names}; atlasbound uninstall --purge takes this repository's part of it, atlasbound leftovers names what a version before {version} left there

setup.last: next: atlasbound doctor  checks what setup wired and ends "doctor: ok"; then restart your AI session
setup.ignoreCommit: commit .gitignore: it holds no machine path
setup.ignoreSame: .gitignore is as it was: nothing to commit
setup.outOfGit: {ignore}; the files that name this machine stay out of git{mcp}
setup.outOfGitMcp: , .mcp.json too: it names this machine's node and install
setup.offHere: {name} is off here (its module is off)
setup.offVerbs: {off}: its verbs are off, the rest works
setup.protectRow: {why}: nothing is protected; atlasbound doctor names it
setup.namedOnly: {name} is installed and not wired: a plain setup leaves it off; the person wires it, in a terminal of their own: atlasbound setup --with {name}
setup.head: atlasbound {verb}: {root}
setup.wired: wired {rows} hooks{servers} in {files} files: {commands} commands and skills, {placed}; restart your AI session so it picks them up
setup.allowed: allowed without a prompt: {n} rules for the commands that only look{mcp} (no write but your AI's drafts in {drafts}; no git rule), in {file}; uninstall takes them out
setup.looseFailed:
commit .gitignore: it holds no machine path
  {says}
setup.retired: removed {key}: this installation no longer has it
setup.retiredKept: kept {key}: this installation no longer has it, and you changed it
setup.restored: restored {key}: you had changed it; your copy is {copy}
setup.retiredHeld: kept {key}: this installation no longer has it, and git holds it, so it is the team's
setup.keptGit: kept {key}: git holds it, so it is the team's
setup.keptStore: kept {key}: {why}; {unignored}git sees it; atlasbound uninstall --purge removes it
setup.keptHome: kept {key}: what this repository left in your home; atlasbound uninstall --purge removes it
setup.keptYours: kept {key}: you changed it, so it is yours now
setup.purge: atlasbound uninstall --purge also deletes, for good: {named}
setup.purgeNothing: nothing more than a plain uninstall takes
setup.tookLines: took our lines out of {key}: the rest of it stays
setup.team: kept {key}: the team's file, setup did not write it
setup.program: to remove the program too: npm uninstall -g atlasbound
setup.joined: set up by your team already (its .gitignore block came with git): this wires this machine only, and what came with git stays as it came
setup.noticePut: team notice: one hook row in {file} tells a teammate whose machine is not set up to install atlasbound, once per session and never in a headless run; commit {file} with .gitignore so they are told; delete that row and commit to switch it off
setup.noticeOlder: team notice: the row in {file} was written by another version; only that row was rewritten, the rest of the file is as it was
setup.noticeAbsent: team notice: {file} holds no team row (set up by an earlier version, or switched off): atlasbound setup --team-notice writes it, then commit {file}
setup.noticeStale: team notice: the row in {file} was written by another version and still works; it stays as committed, and atlasbound setup --team-notice rewrites only that row
setup.noticeUnread: team notice: {file} does not read as JSON, so it was not touched
setup.noticeKept: kept the team notice in {key}: it came with git and is the team's; to switch it off for everyone, delete that row and commit
setup.fromGit: kept our lines in {key}: it came with git as it is, so it is the team's; take them out and commit to change that for everyone

doctor.notOn: its module is not on here
doctor.noModule: no module is wired here: atlasbound setup
doctor.wireAgain: fix: atlasbound update (it wires this repository for the installed version; atlasbound setup where it was never set up)
doctor.goneMore: not wired: {n} more, atlasbound debug doctor lists them
doctor.config: config refused: {says}: this view read the shipped config; every other verb refuses until the file reads
doctor.promised: capabilities: the code of {answering} of {n} verbs, hooks and tools the product promises answers (wiring: the rows above; debug doctor lists each)
doctor.head: atlasbound doctor: {root}
doctor.noModuleRow: no module is wired here: atlasbound setup

modules.notSetUp: this repository is not set up: atlasbound setup, or setup --only <modules>

turnsOn.off: only the person turns it back on, in a terminal of their own: atlasbound modules on {name}

modules.plainOff: ; a plain setup leaves {name} off, the person's setup --with {name} wires it
modules.onHere: on here: {on}; restart your AI session so it picks this up

protect.what: AtlasBound can protect your source files: before an AI edits a protected file, it first writes a short plan with DecisionBook (why, which files, how it is checked) and asks you to approve it. It cannot prove who typed the yes, and it is a check, not a sandbox: it sees an AI's write tools and what a shell command's text says it writes, never what a program does once it runs.
protect.later: you can change this any time with atlasbound protect
forTheAi: protect your source files? (for the AI: ask the person; do not answer this yourself)
choose: the paths the person names  ->  atlasbound protect "<path or glob>[,...]"
not now: nothing is protected  ->  the person types atlasbound protect --none in their own terminal
protect.noAnswer: protect: no answer, so nothing is protected yet; setup asks again next time

drafts.both: --file, or the JSON as a word: not both ({words})
drafts.outside: {given}: a draft is read only from {drafts} in {root}
drafts.none: {given}: no draft there; write it with your Write tool first
drafts.kept: the draft stays at {key}: fix it with your Edit tool (never sed or a script: the host asks the person for those), then run the same call again

release.noManifest: no {manifest}: a checkout, not a release

probes.notStarted: the quoted command did not start: {why}
probes.wider: ~/{key} is open to others ({mode}), wider than private (700): the product's next write there tightens it
probes.noHome: this user has no home in the system's user record
probes.pathUnknown: {product} on PATH is {seen}; this install states no version
probes.pathOther: {product} on PATH is {seen}, this install is {version}: install {product} {version} again
probes.noHookRow: not wired: no hook row in the settings
probes.notFired: no hook has fired here yet; restart the AI session so the host picks them up
probes.noStore: not wired: the server would make a folder here for its trace
probes.noGateRow: not wired: no gate row in the settings
probes.notOurs: not measured: a row not ours
probes.noGate: not measured: no module on here gates an edit
probes.answered: the port answered {verdict} for a file no plan names ({gates} {reads} it){asks}
probes.noIgnored: not wired: none of the files setup keeps out of git is here
probes.ignored: git ignores the {n} files setup keeps out of it
probes.lacks: not measured, what this machine lacks: {code}
probes.noticeOn: in {file}, {committed}: a teammate whose machine is not set up is told once per session to install atlasbound
probes.noticeLoose: not committed yet (commit it so teammates are told)
probes.noticeOld: in {file}, written by another version (still works); atlasbound setup --team-notice rewrites only that row
probes.noticeNone: off: {file} holds none, so a teammate whose machine is not set up is not told; to tell them: atlasbound setup --team-notice, then commit {file}

adapters.tasks: tasks: the question, the command, the fields to read
adapters.boundStart: the directory it was given or started in
adapters.noBackground: debug inject starts no background work
adapters.scriptUsage: debug inject --script <file.json>: a JSON list of host events
adapters.noTranscript: debug inject: the transcript {name} is not beside the script

help.phrase: , after typing the phrase it shows ({phrase} ...)

help.whoPerson: only you, at your own terminal{phrase}; an AI session is refused
help.takesOut: ; taking a module out, or turning on again one that is off here (--only, --without or --with where it is set up), is yours only
help.whoAi: your AI session (you may run it too)
help.setup: connect this repository to your AI session; it asks you what to protect
help.then: then restart your AI session, so it loads the hooks{slash}

typed.flagAlone: {flag}; with no command AtlasBound takes {some} and {last}
typed.jsonBreaks: the JSON breaks at line {line}, column {column}

choice.noneLeft: that choice leaves no module on; uninstall takes everything out
choice.lastOn: {name} is the last module on here; atlasbound uninstall takes everything out

hooks.stopHeld: atlasbound: a deliberate check, not a crash: the session was held from finishing and the AI was told what to do first

inject.silent: events that said nothing: {silent} of {events}; said {said}, held {held}

shell.maybe: , a file only where the disk holds one
shell.oneWord: debug shell takes the command as one quoted word
shell.nothing: no file written: nothing for a gate to judge
shell.setsHost: a variable the host sets for the session
shell.hostEnv: sets {names}: the shell gate denies the command (shell-host-env), whatever it writes

trace.onlyLooked: no work run yet: only runs that looked
trace.newerLooked: a newer run only looked: {verb} at {at}Z; atlasbound debug trace {run} shows it
trace.noPackage: no record of package {pkg} here; the records are of {pkgs}

who.aiShell: a shell command of an AI session
